tables.name: campuses
tables.description: University campuses: every campus groups buildings and students.

tables.name: buildings
tables.description: Buildings of each campus. One-to-many relation with campuses by id_campus.

tables.name: classrooms
tables.description: Classrooms of each building. One-to-many relation with buildings by id_building.

fields.name: floor
fields.description: Floor of the building (0 = ground floor)

tables.name: teachers
tables.description: Teaching staff. One-to-many relation with subjects by id_teacher.

fields.name: is_researcher
fields.description: Does the teacher belong to a research group?

tables.name: degrees
tables.description: Degrees. One-to-many relation with subjects by code (text) and with students.

tables.name: subjects
tables.description: Subjects of each degree, taught by a teacher. Two one-to-many relations.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Language it is taught in (may be missing)

tables.name: students
tables.description: Students: each one belongs to a degree and to a campus. One-to-many relation with enrollments.

fields.name: degree_code
fields.description: Degree the student is enrolled in (→ degrees.code)

fields.name: has_scholarship
fields.description: Does the student have a scholarship?

fields.name: id_campus
fields.description: Campus where the student studies (→ campuses.id_campus)

tables.name: enrollments
tables.description: Enrollments: they break the many-to-many relation students ↔ subjects into two one-to-many. The grade is null while the subject is active or cancelled.

fields.name: grade
fields.description: Final grade (null when it is not graded)

fields.name: is_recognised
fields.description: Was the subject recognised from another degree?

queries.name: A01 · All campuses
queries.description: SELECT * over campuses: the columns in table order and the 4 rows by identifier.
queries.sql: SELECT * FROM campuses ORDER BY id_campus

queries.name: A02 · Projection with aliases and arithmetic
queries.description: Divides the capacity by 1000 and sorts by capacity descending: the 4 campuses from largest to smallest.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS campus, city, max_capacity / 1000 AS capacity_thousands, founded_year FROM campuses ORDER BY max_capacity DESC

queries.name: A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)
queries.description: Numeric filter with >= and order by capacity descending and code: 5 classrooms.
queries.sql: SELECT code, capacity, floor FROM classrooms WHERE capacity >= 55 ORDER BY capacity DESC, code

queries.name: A04 · Classrooms with a projector
queries.description: Boolean filter (has_projector = true): 10 classrooms sorted by capacity.
queries.sql: SELECT code, capacity FROM classrooms WHERE has_projector = true ORDER BY capacity DESC, code

queries.name: A05 · Teachers who do not research and have a heavy load
queries.description: AND of a boolean (false) and a range (>= 10 h): 3 teachers.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, category, weekly_hours FROM teachers WHERE is_researcher = false AND weekly_hours >= 10 ORDER BY weekly_hours DESC, last_name

queries.name: A06 · Students with no phone
queries.description: IS NULL over a field with gaps: 8 students.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name FROM students WHERE phone IS NULL ORDER BY last_name

queries.name: A07 · Teachers with an office (IS NOT NULL) in upper case
queries.description: IS NOT NULL plus UPPER over two columns: 9 teachers with an office, the 3 associates without one are left out.
queries.sql: SELECT id_teacher, UPPER(name) AS name, UPPER(last_name) AS last_name, office FROM teachers WHERE office IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id_teacher

queries.name: A08 · Last names that start with G
queries.description: LIKE with a trailing wildcard: 3 students called García, Gómez and Guerrero.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name FROM students WHERE last_name LIKE 'G%' ORDER BY id_student

queries.name: A09 · Institutional addresses that do not start with a
queries.description: LIKE and NOT LIKE combined with LIMIT 5 over the sorted address.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, email FROM students WHERE email LIKE '%@alu.es' AND email NOT LIKE 'a%' ORDER BY email LIMIT 5

queries.name: A10 · Three given classrooms (IN) and the remainder of the division
queries.description: IN with a list of codes and the remainder operator (%): the remainder of dividing the capacity by 10.
queries.sql: SELECT code, capacity, capacity % 10 AS remainder FROM classrooms WHERE code IN ('K-101', 'B-SALA', 'M-001') ORDER BY code

queries.name: A11 · Degrees that are neither computing nor education (NOT IN)
queries.description: NOT IN with three codes: Data Science, Software Engineering and Law are left.
queries.sql: SELECT code, name, level FROM degrees WHERE code NOT IN ('GINF', 'GMED', 'GEDU') ORDER BY code

queries.name: A12 · Enrollments passed with a grade between 7 and 8 (BETWEEN)
queries.description: BETWEEN includes the ends: 12 enrollments with a grade of 7, 7.5 or 8, sorted by grade.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade BETWEEN 7 AND 8 ORDER BY grade, id_enrollment

queries.name: A13 · First and second year subjects with few credits
queries.description: Parentheses with OR, a boolean and NOT BETWEEN: 9 compulsory subjects of years 1 and 2 with fewer than 7 credits.
queries.sql: SELECT name, year, credits FROM subjects WHERE (year = 1 OR year = 2) AND is_compulsory = true AND credits NOT BETWEEN 7 AND 10 ORDER BY name

queries.name: A14 · Teacher categories (DISTINCT)
queries.description: DISTINCT over a text column: 4 professional categories.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM teachers ORDER BY category

queries.name: A15 · Level/officialness combinations (DISTINCT of two columns)
queries.description: DISTINCT over two columns, a boolean included: 3 combinations.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT level, is_official FROM degrees ORDER BY level, is_official

queries.name: A16 · Totals of the records (COUNT, DISTINCT, MIN, MAX, SUM)
queries.description: Aggregates with no GROUP BY: 48 enrollments, 32 graded, 21 students and 14 subjects with enrollments.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS enrollments, COUNT(grade) AS with_grade, COUNT(DISTINCT id_student) AS students, COUNT(DISTINCT id_subject) AS subjects, MIN(grade) AS min_grade, MAX(grade) AS max_grade, SUM(grade) AS grade_sum FROM enrollments

queries.name: A17 · Enrollments by status
queries.description: GROUP BY with two aggregates: the 13 active and the 3 cancelled have no grade, the 32 passed do.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(grade) AS graded FROM enrollments GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC, status

queries.name: A18 · Enrollments by academic year (HAVING)
queries.description: GROUP BY with HAVING COUNT(*) > 20: both years go over the threshold.
queries.sql: SELECT academic_year, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY academic_year HAVING COUNT(*) > 20 ORDER BY academic_year

queries.name: A19 · Students with three or more enrollments
queries.description: GROUP BY over the M:M plus HAVING >= 3: 10 students, one of them with 4 enrollments.
queries.sql: SELECT id_student, COUNT(*) AS enrollments FROM enrollments GROUP BY id_student HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY enrollments DESC, id_student

queries.name: A20 · Classrooms by the first letter of the code (GROUP BY with an expression)
queries.description: GROUP BY over SUBSTR: 7 different initials with their number of classrooms and added seats.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(code, 1, 1) AS initial, COUNT(*) AS classrooms, SUM(capacity) AS seats FROM classrooms GROUP BY SUBSTR(code, 1, 1) ORDER BY initial

queries.name: A21 · Grades of subject 6, from highest to lowest (NULLS LAST)
queries.description: ORDER BY ... DESC NULLS LAST: the cancelled enrollment with no grade goes last.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, grade FROM enrollments WHERE id_subject = 6 ORDER BY grade DESC NULLS LAST, id_enrollment

queries.name: A22 · Grades of subject 6, from lowest to highest (nulls first)
queries.description: In ASC the nulls go first by default: the enrollment with no grade heads the result.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, grade FROM enrollments WHERE id_subject = 6 ORDER BY grade ASC, id_enrollment

queries.name: A23 · Oldest students, page 2 (LIMIT/OFFSET)
queries.description: It sorts by date of birth and skips the first two rows: 4 rows from the third one on.
queries.sql: SELECT name, last_name, birth_date FROM students ORDER BY birth_date LIMIT 4 OFFSET 2

queries.name: A24 · Four students starting at the fourth (MySQL style LIMIT)
queries.description: LIMIT 3, 4 is the same as OFFSET 3 LIMIT 4: it returns identifiers 4 to 7.
queries.sql: SELECT id_student, name FROM students ORDER BY id_student LIMIT 3, 4

queries.name: A25 · Record of three students (concatenation and text functions)
queries.description: || concatenates, LENGTH counts characters and SUBSTR trims: last names in upper case and three initials.
queries.sql: SELECT UPPER(last_name) || ', ' || name AS record, LENGTH(name) AS letters, SUBSTR(name, 1, 3) AS initials FROM students WHERE id_student IN (1, 9, 14) ORDER BY id_student

queries.name: A26 · Missing grades: COALESCE, IFNULL, NULLIF and ROUND
queries.description: The null values are replaced by -1 and 0; NULLIF turns «cancelled» into null and the distance to 7.5 spreads the null.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, COALESCE(grade, -1) AS grade_coalesce, IFNULL(grade, 0) AS grade_ifnull, NULLIF(status, 'cancelled') AS status_or_null, ROUND(ABS(grade - 7.5), 2) AS distance FROM enrollments WHERE id_enrollment IN (2, 6, 28, 30, 48) ORDER BY id_enrollment

queries.name: A27 · Campus phone normalised
queries.description: IFNULL + TRIM + NULLIF: the campus with no phone returns null instead of an empty string.
queries.sql: SELECT id_campus, NULLIF(TRIM(IFNULL(phone, '')), '') AS phone, name FROM campuses ORDER BY id_campus

queries.name: A28 · Boards that are not digital (comment and brackets)
queries.description: The -- comment is ignored, [code] is the same as code and <> also discards the nulls.
queries.sql:
-- Classrooms with a chalk board (those with an unknown board do not count)
SELECT [code] AS classroom, [board_type] AS board, capacity FROM classrooms WHERE board_type <> 'digital' ORDER BY code

queries.name: A29 · Teachers who are not associates (NOT)
queries.description: NOT over an equality: 9 of the 12 teachers are left.
queries.sql: SELECT name, category FROM teachers WHERE NOT (category = 'Associate') ORDER BY id_teacher

queries.name: A30 · A query with no results
queries.description: No classroom goes over 200 seats: the result has the columns and zero rows (rowCount 0).
queries.sql: SELECT code FROM classrooms WHERE capacity > 200

queries.name: A31 · Average grade per subject (HAVING and ORDER BY by alias)
queries.description: Only subjects with two or more grades; it sorts by the average and a tie is broken by identifier.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, COUNT(*) AS enrollments, COUNT(grade) AS graded, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM enrollments GROUP BY id_subject HAVING COUNT(grade) >= 2 ORDER BY average_grade DESC, id_subject

queries.name: A32 · Students and addresses per campus
queries.description: GROUP BY id_campus with COUNT(*) and COUNT(email): 18 of the 24 students have an address.
queries.sql: SELECT id_campus, COUNT(*) AS students, COUNT(email) AS with_email FROM students GROUP BY id_campus ORDER BY id_campus

queries.name: A33 · Records with CONCAT (text and numbers)
queries.description: Joins name and surname with CONCAT, and the degree code with the identifier: the first 7 students by identifier. The contact is null when there is no email.
queries.sql: SELECT CONCAT(name, ' ', last_name) AS student, CONCAT(degree_code, '-', id_student) AS enrollment_code, CONCAT(degree_code, ' · ', email) AS contact FROM students ORDER BY id_student LIMIT 7

queries.name: A34 · Global totals with every aggregate (no GROUP BY)
queries.description: Aggregates without GROUP BY, one of each kind: 48 enrollments, 32 graded, 21 students and 3 different statuses; total 234, minimum 5, maximum 10 and rounded average 7.31.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS enrollments, COUNT(grade) AS graded, COUNT(DISTINCT id_student) AS students, COUNT(DISTINCT status) AS statuses, SUM(grade) AS total_grade, MIN(grade) AS minimum, MAX(grade) AS maximum, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrollments

queries.name: A35 · Every aggregate by status (GROUP BY)
queries.description: GROUP BY status with COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT), SUM, MIN, MAX and AVG: only the 32 passed have grades; active and cancelled give NULL in the grade aggregates.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(DISTINCT id_student) AS students, SUM(grade) AS total_grade, MIN(grade) AS minimum, MAX(grade) AS maximum, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrollments GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC, status

queries.name: A36 · Subjects with four enrollments and a high average (double HAVING)
queries.description: HAVING with two aggregates at once: subjects with at least 4 enrollments and an average of 7 or more; four subjects meet both thresholds.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, COUNT(*) AS enrollments, COUNT(grade) AS graded, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrollments GROUP BY id_subject HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 AND AVG(grade) >= 7 ORDER BY average DESC, id_subject

queries.name: A37 · Students and contact details per campus (COUNT of columns with NULL)
queries.description: COUNT(*) counts rows and COUNT(column) only the non-null values: campus 2 has 6 students but fewer e-mails and phones. HAVING keeps the campuses with 5 students or more.
queries.sql: SELECT id_campus, COUNT(*) AS students, COUNT(email) AS with_email, COUNT(phone) AS with_phone FROM students GROUP BY id_campus HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY students DESC, id_campus

queries.name: A38 · Teachers by category with distinct offices (HAVING COUNT DISTINCT)
queries.description: COUNT(office) ignores nulls and COUNT(DISTINCT office) counts distinct offices: the three assistant teachers have no office and are filtered out by the HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS teachers, COUNT(office) AS with_office, COUNT(DISTINCT office) AS offices FROM teachers GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT office) >= 2 ORDER BY offices DESC, category

queries.name: A39 · Enrollments by academic year and status (GROUP BY of two columns)
queries.description: Grouping by two columns with HAVING: only two combinations reach 10 enrollments; the active one has no grades and its total is NULL.
queries.sql: SELECT academic_year, status, COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(grade) AS total_grade FROM enrollments GROUP BY academic_year, status HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY academic_year, status

queries.name: A40 · Subjects averaging above 7.5 among graded enrollments (WHERE and HAVING)
queries.description: WHERE removes enrollments without a grade before grouping and HAVING filters the groups by their average: four subjects remain, one of them with a single grade.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, COUNT(*) AS enrollments, ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY id_subject HAVING AVG(grade) > 7.5 ORDER BY average DESC, id_subject

queries.name: A41 · Classrooms per floor with SUM, MIN and MAX (HAVING SUM)
queries.description: Per floor, COUNT(*), SUM, MIN and MAX of the capacity; HAVING keeps the floors adding up to 100 seats or more.
queries.sql: SELECT floor, COUNT(*) AS classrooms, SUM(capacity) AS seats, MIN(capacity) AS minimum, MAX(capacity) AS maximum FROM classrooms GROUP BY floor HAVING SUM(capacity) >= 100 ORDER BY seats DESC

queries.name: A42 · Weekly teacher hours by category with MIN, MAX and AVG (HAVING AVG)
queries.description: MIN, MAX and rounded AVG of the weekly hours by category; the HAVING requires an average of 10 hours or more.
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS teachers, MIN(weekly_hours) AS min_hours, MAX(weekly_hours) AS max_hours, ROUND(AVG(weekly_hours), 1) AS average_hours FROM teachers GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(weekly_hours) >= 10 ORDER BY average_hours DESC

queries.name: A43 · Students by birth year (GROUP BY with an expression and HAVING)
queries.description: GROUP BY on the year of the date (SUBSTR) with COUNT(*) and COUNT(phone); HAVING requires at least two students per year.
queries.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(birth_date, 1, 4) AS year, COUNT(*) AS students, COUNT(phone) AS with_phone FROM students GROUP BY SUBSTR(birth_date, 1, 4) HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY year

queries.name: A44 · Aggregates over the grouped column itself (COUNT of status)
queries.description: Aggregates over the grouped column and over others: COUNT(status) matches COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT status) is 1; graded only shows up in the passed rows.
queries.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(status) AS with_status, COUNT(DISTINCT status) AS statuses, MAX(id_enrollment) AS last_id, COUNT(grade) AS graded FROM enrollments GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC, status

queries.name: A45 · HAVING with aggregates that are not in the SELECT
queries.description: The HAVING uses COUNT(*) and SUM(grade), which do not appear in the SELECT: only the passed enrollments meet both thresholds.
queries.sql: SELECT status FROM enrollments GROUP BY status HAVING COUNT(*) >= 13 AND SUM(grade) > 200 ORDER BY status

queries.name: A46 · Students with an e-mail per campus (WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING)
queries.description: WHERE filters before grouping: per campus, COUNT(*) of students with an institutional e-mail and COUNT(phone) of those with a phone; HAVING requires 4 or more.
queries.sql: SELECT id_campus, COUNT(*) AS students, COUNT(phone) AS with_phone FROM students WHERE email LIKE '%@alu.es' GROUP BY id_campus HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 ORDER BY students DESC, id_campus

queries.name: B01 · Campuses with their buildings (INNER JOIN)
queries.description: 1:M join by id_campus: the 8 buildings with the name of their campus, sorted by campus and building.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS campus, e.name AS building, e.floors, e.has_lift FROM campuses AS s INNER JOIN buildings AS e ON e.id_campus = s.id_campus ORDER BY s.id_campus, e.id_building

queries.name: B02 · Three tables: large classrooms of campus 1
queries.description: campuses → buildings → classrooms with a filter by campus and capacity: 3 classrooms, from largest to smallest.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS campus, e.name AS building, a.code, a.capacity FROM campuses AS s INNER JOIN buildings AS e ON e.id_campus = s.id_campus INNER JOIN classrooms AS a ON a.id_building = e.id_building WHERE s.id_campus = 1 AND a.capacity >= 45 ORDER BY a.capacity DESC, a.code

queries.name: B03 · Campuses with no buildings (LEFT JOIN with no pair)
queries.description: LEFT JOIN plus IS NULL: the 4 campuses have buildings, so the result is empty.
queries.sql: SELECT s.name AS campus FROM campuses AS s LEFT JOIN buildings AS e ON e.id_campus = s.id_campus WHERE e.id_building IS NULL ORDER BY s.id_campus

queries.name: B03b · Buildings with no classrooms
queries.description: LEFT JOIN with IS NULL: only the Sports Pavilion is left with no classrooms.
queries.sql: SELECT e.id_building, e.name FROM buildings AS e LEFT JOIN classrooms AS a ON a.id_building = e.id_building WHERE a.id_classroom IS NULL ORDER BY e.id_building

queries.name: B04 · Teachers with no subjects
queries.description: LEFT JOIN teachers → subjects with IS NULL: 3 associates teach no subject.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_teacher, d.name, d.last_name FROM teachers AS d LEFT JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_teacher = d.id_teacher WHERE a.id_subject IS NULL ORDER BY d.id_teacher

queries.name: B05 · Implicit join with commas (classrooms of campus 2)
queries.description: FROM classrooms, buildings with the equality in the WHERE: the engine resolves it as a join.
queries.sql: SELECT a.code, a.capacity, e.name AS building FROM classrooms AS a, buildings AS e WHERE a.id_building = e.id_building AND e.id_campus = 2 ORDER BY a.id_classroom

queries.name: B06 · Subjects and credits per degree (join by a text code)
queries.description: Join by degrees.code = subjects.degree_code, with COUNT and SUM per degree.
queries.sql: SELECT e.code, e.name AS degree, COUNT(a.id_subject) AS subjects, SUM(a.credits) AS credits FROM degrees AS e INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.degree_code = e.code GROUP BY e.code, e.name ORDER BY credits DESC, e.code

queries.name: B07 · Degrees with at least three subjects (LEFT JOIN + HAVING)
queries.description: LEFT JOIN with HAVING COUNT >= 3: Computer Engineering, Primary Education and Medicine.
queries.sql: SELECT e.code, e.name AS degree, COUNT(a.id_subject) AS subjects FROM degrees AS e LEFT JOIN subjects AS a ON a.degree_code = e.code GROUP BY e.code, e.name HAVING COUNT(a.id_subject) >= 3 ORDER BY subjects DESC, e.code

queries.name: B08 · Classrooms and seats per building
queries.description: Grouping by building with COUNT and SUM: the Pythagoras Lecture Hall heads it with 150 seats.
queries.sql: SELECT e.id_building, e.name AS building, COUNT(a.id_classroom) AS classrooms, SUM(a.capacity) AS seats FROM buildings AS e INNER JOIN classrooms AS a ON a.id_building = e.id_building GROUP BY e.id_building, e.name ORDER BY seats DESC, e.id_building

queries.name: B09 · Classrooms per building, including those with none (LEFT JOIN)
queries.description: LEFT JOIN with COUNT: the Sports Pavilion appears with 0 classrooms.
queries.sql: SELECT e.id_building, e.name AS building, COUNT(a.id_classroom) AS classrooms FROM buildings AS e LEFT JOIN classrooms AS a ON a.id_building = e.id_building GROUP BY e.id_building, e.name ORDER BY classrooms ASC, e.id_building

queries.name: B10 · Teaching load: subjects and classroom hours
queries.description: teachers → subjects with COUNT and SUM: Elena and Carmen go over 145 hours.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_teacher, d.name, COUNT(a.id_subject) AS subjects, SUM(a.classroom_hours) AS hours FROM teachers AS d INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_teacher = d.id_teacher GROUP BY d.id_teacher, d.name ORDER BY hours DESC, d.id_teacher

queries.name: B11 · Teachers with two subjects and 12 credits or more (double HAVING)
queries.description: HAVING with COUNT and SUM at once: only Carmen, Elena and Marc make the cut.
queries.sql: SELECT d.id_teacher, d.last_name, COUNT(*) AS subjects, SUM(a.credits) AS credits FROM teachers AS d INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_teacher = d.id_teacher GROUP BY d.id_teacher, d.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 AND SUM(a.credits) >= 12 ORDER BY credits DESC, d.id_teacher

queries.name: B12 · Subjects with no language set, with their degree and teacher
queries.description: Three tables (subjects + degrees + teachers) and IS NULL over the language.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.name AS subject, e.name AS degree, d.last_name AS teacher, a.credits FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = a.degree_code INNER JOIN teachers AS d ON d.id_teacher = a.id_teacher WHERE a.language IS NULL ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: B13 · Students, addresses and phones per campus
queries.description: LEFT JOIN campuses → students with three counts: 18 addresses and 16 phones in all.
queries.sql: SELECT s.id_campus, s.name AS campus, COUNT(e.id_student) AS students, COUNT(e.email) AS with_email, COUNT(e.phone) AS with_phone FROM campuses AS s LEFT JOIN students AS e ON e.id_campus = s.id_campus GROUP BY s.id_campus, s.name ORDER BY students DESC, s.id_campus

queries.name: B14 · Cartesian product (6 degrees × 4 campuses)
queries.description: With no join condition you get every combination; LIMIT 6 shows the first ones.
queries.sql: SELECT e.code, s.name AS campus FROM degrees AS e, campuses AS s ORDER BY e.code, s.id_campus LIMIT 6

queries.name: B15 · The five largest classrooms (JOIN + ORDER BY alias + LIMIT)
queries.description: It sorts by the alias of a column and by the classroom code; the tie at 55 seats is decided by the classroom.
queries.sql: SELECT a.code AS classroom, a.capacity AS seats, e.name AS building FROM classrooms AS a INNER JOIN buildings AS e ON e.id_building = a.id_building ORDER BY seats DESC, classroom LIMIT 5

queries.name: B16 · Distinct teachers per degree (COUNT DISTINCT)
queries.description: COUNT(DISTINCT id_teacher) per degree: Computer Engineering is the one that spreads its teaching over more teachers.
queries.sql: SELECT e.code, COUNT(DISTINCT a.id_teacher) AS distinct_teachers, COUNT(*) AS subjects FROM degrees AS e INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.degree_code = e.code GROUP BY e.code ORDER BY distinct_teachers DESC, e.code

queries.name: B17 · Teaching hours per category (MIN and MAX)
queries.description: GROUP BY category with a count and the extremes: senior lecturers are the most numerous.
queries.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS teachers, MIN(weekly_hours) AS min_hours, MAX(weekly_hours) AS max_hours FROM teachers GROUP BY category ORDER BY teachers DESC, category

queries.name: B18 · Basic subjects of years one and two with their teacher
queries.description: Join teachers → subjects with BETWEEN, >= and a boolean in the WHERE: 8 subjects.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name, d.last_name, a.name AS subject, a.year FROM teachers AS d INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_teacher = d.id_teacher WHERE a.year BETWEEN 1 AND 2 AND a.credits >= 6 AND a.is_compulsory = true ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: B19 · Enrollments and average grade per level (Bachelor / Master)
queries.description: Four tables and ROUND(AVG()): masters raise the average of the bachelor (43 enrollments against 5).
queries.sql: SELECT e.level, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id_enrollment) AS enrollments, ROUND(AVG(m.grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM degrees AS e INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.degree_code = e.code INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject GROUP BY e.level ORDER BY average_grade DESC

queries.name: B20 · Optional subjects and their degree
queries.description: Boolean filter (is_compulsory = false) over the join degrees ↔ subjects: 5 optional subjects.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.name, e.name AS degree, a.language FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = a.degree_code WHERE a.is_compulsory = false ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: B21 · Master students with their degree
queries.description: Join students → degrees by the text code, filtering by level Master: 4 students.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, st.name, st.last_name, e.name AS degree, e.level FROM students AS st INNER JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = st.degree_code WHERE e.level = 'Master' ORDER BY st.id_student

queries.name: B22 · Daily schedule of the research staff
queries.description: Boolean filter and ROUND over a division, sorted by weekly hours: 6 researchers.
queries.sql: SELECT d.name, d.weekly_hours, ROUND(d.weekly_hours / 5, 1) AS hours_per_day FROM teachers AS d WHERE d.is_researcher = true ORDER BY d.weekly_hours DESC, d.id_teacher

queries.name: C01 · Full record of one student (M:M resolved)
queries.description: Three tables over the M:M: the 4 subjects of Ana, with grade and status.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_enrollment, st.last_name AS student, a.name AS subject, m.grade, m.status FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE m.id_student = 1 ORDER BY m.id_enrollment

queries.name: C02 · Subjects with four or more students (large group)
queries.description: It walks the M:M from subject → enrollments and groups with HAVING >= 4: 8 subjects.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.name AS subject, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id_student) AS students FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject GROUP BY a.id_subject, a.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m.id_student) >= 4 ORDER BY students DESC, a.id_subject

queries.name: C03 · Load of every student (subjects and credits)
queries.description: The other side of the M:M: 21 students with enrollments, sorted by credits and breaking ties by identifier.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, st.name, st.last_name, COUNT(*) AS subjects, SUM(a.credits) AS credits FROM students AS st INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject GROUP BY st.id_student, st.name, st.last_name ORDER BY credits DESC, st.id_student

queries.name: C04 · Grades of one student with COALESCE
queries.description: COALESCE turns the null of the active subject into 0 instead of leaving it empty.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject, m.status, COALESCE(m.grade, 0) AS grade FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE m.id_student = 4 ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: C05 · Enrollments not graded yet (IS NULL)
queries.description: The first six enrollments with no grade, with student and subject.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_enrollment, st.last_name AS student, a.name AS subject, m.status FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE m.grade IS NULL ORDER BY m.id_enrollment LIMIT 6

queries.name: C06 · Enrollments with distinction (grade >= 9)
queries.description: Six enrollments of 9 or more, from the highest grade down and breaking ties by student.
queries.sql: SELECT st.last_name AS student, a.name AS subject, m.grade FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE m.grade >= 9 ORDER BY m.grade DESC, st.id_student

queries.name: C07 · Students with no enrollment (LEFT JOIN and null average)
queries.description: Three students have no enrollments: COUNT is 0 and ROUND(AVG()) is null.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, st.name, st.last_name, COUNT(m.id_enrollment) AS enrollments, ROUND(AVG(m.grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM students AS st LEFT JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student GROUP BY st.id_student, st.name, st.last_name HAVING COUNT(m.id_enrollment) = 0 ORDER BY st.id_student

queries.name: C08 · Subjects with no enrollment
queries.description: LEFT JOIN with IS NULL: Testing and Quality and Business Law are left with no students.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.name, a.degree_code FROM subjects AS a LEFT JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject WHERE m.id_enrollment IS NULL ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: C09 · Coverage: students with enrollments per degree
queries.description: Four tables (degrees → subjects → enrollments → students) to count the real students of every degree.
queries.sql: SELECT e.code, COUNT(DISTINCT st.id_student) AS students FROM degrees AS e INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.degree_code = e.code INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject INNER JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student GROUP BY e.code ORDER BY students DESC, e.code

queries.name: C10 · Nobody takes subjects of two degrees (only rowCount)
queries.description: An assert with no expected rows: it is enough to check that the result is empty (rowCount 0).
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, COUNT(DISTINCT a.degree_code) AS degrees FROM students AS st INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject GROUP BY st.id_student HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.degree_code) >= 2 ORDER BY st.id_student

queries.name: C11 · Recognised enrollments
queries.description: Boolean is_recognised = true over the M:M: 6 enrollments, one per student.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_enrollment, st.last_name AS student, a.name AS subject, e.code AS degree FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject INNER JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = a.degree_code WHERE m.is_recognised = true ORDER BY m.id_enrollment

queries.name: C12 · Subjects of one student whatever the order (ignoreOrder)
queries.description: The assert does not sort: it checks that the set of rows matches, with ignoreOrder true.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject WHERE m.id_student = 4

queries.name: C13 · Subjects with more enrollments (ORDER BY of an aggregate)
queries.description: It sorts by COUNT(*) descending and cuts the first five: three subjects tie at 5 enrollments.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject, COUNT(*) AS enrollments FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject GROUP BY a.name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, a.name LIMIT 5

queries.name: C14 · Longest subject names (ORDER BY of a function)
queries.description: It sorts by LENGTH(name) descending, not by the text: 5 rows.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject, LENGTH(a.name) AS letters FROM subjects AS a ORDER BY LENGTH(a.name) DESC, a.name LIMIT 5

queries.name: C15 · Students with more credits enrolled (ORDER BY alias + LIMIT)
queries.description: It sorts by the alias credits: Ana heads it with 24 credits and the rest tie at 19.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, st.last_name, COUNT(*) AS subjects, SUM(a.credits) AS credits FROM students AS st INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject GROUP BY st.id_student, st.last_name ORDER BY credits DESC, st.id_student LIMIT 4

queries.name: C16 · Average grade of the Computing subjects
queries.description: Filter by degree code, aggregates and NULLS LAST: the subject with no grade goes last.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject, COUNT(m.id_enrollment) AS enrollments, COUNT(m.grade) AS graded, ROUND(AVG(m.grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM subjects AS a INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_subject = a.id_subject WHERE a.degree_code = 'GINF' GROUP BY a.id_subject, a.name ORDER BY average_grade DESC NULLS LAST, a.id_subject

queries.name: C17 · Scholarship holders in Human Anatomy
queries.description: A student boolean and a subject filter over the M:M: 2 of the 4 enrolled have a scholarship.
queries.sql: SELECT st.last_name AS student, st.has_scholarship, a.name AS subject FROM students AS st INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE st.has_scholarship = true AND m.id_subject = 5 ORDER BY st.id_student

queries.name: C18 · Enrollments per degree and academic year
queries.description: GROUP BY with two text keys: 12 combinations, in degree + year order.
queries.sql: SELECT a.degree_code, m.academic_year, COUNT(*) AS enrollments FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject GROUP BY a.degree_code, m.academic_year ORDER BY a.degree_code, m.academic_year

queries.name: C19 · Subjects with distinctions
queries.description: Grade filter and GROUP BY: Data Structures is the only one with two distinctions.
queries.sql: SELECT a.name AS subject, COUNT(*) AS outstanding FROM enrollments AS m INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE m.grade >= 9 GROUP BY a.name ORDER BY outstanding DESC, a.name

queries.name: C20 · Average per Computing student with two or more grades
queries.description: Four tables, IS NOT NULL and HAVING COUNT >= 2: Ana and Sara go over 7.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student, st.last_name, ROUND(AVG(m.grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM students AS st INNER JOIN enrollments AS m ON m.id_student = st.id_student INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject INNER JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = a.degree_code WHERE e.code = 'GINF' AND m.grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY st.id_student, st.last_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY average_grade DESC, st.id_student

queries.name: D01 · Enrollments with no student (integrity of the 1:M)
queries.description: Anti-join enrollments → students: no enrollment points to a student that does not exist.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_enrollment, m.id_student FROM enrollments AS m LEFT JOIN students AS st ON st.id_student = m.id_student WHERE st.id_student IS NULL ORDER BY m.id_enrollment

queries.name: D02 · Enrollments with no subject (integrity of the other 1:M)
queries.description: Anti-join enrollments → subjects: the M:M has no dangling references.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_enrollment, m.id_subject FROM enrollments AS m LEFT JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = m.id_subject WHERE a.id_subject IS NULL ORDER BY m.id_enrollment

queries.name: D03 · Subjects with no degree (integrity of the text code)
queries.description: Anti-join subjects → degrees by degree_code = code: the 16 subjects have a degree.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.degree_code FROM subjects AS a LEFT JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = a.degree_code WHERE e.id_degree IS NULL ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: D04 · Subjects with no teacher
queries.description: Anti-join subjects → teachers: every subject has a teacher.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_subject, a.id_teacher FROM subjects AS a LEFT JOIN teachers AS d ON d.id_teacher = a.id_teacher WHERE d.id_teacher IS NULL ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: D05 · Classrooms with no building
queries.description: Anti-join classrooms → buildings: no classroom is left outside a building.
queries.sql: SELECT a.id_classroom, a.id_building FROM classrooms AS a LEFT JOIN buildings AS e ON e.id_building = a.id_building WHERE e.id_building IS NULL ORDER BY a.id_classroom

queries.name: D06 · Buildings with no campus
queries.description: Anti-join buildings → campuses: the 8 buildings hang from an existing campus.
queries.sql: SELECT e.id_building, e.id_campus FROM buildings AS e LEFT JOIN campuses AS s ON s.id_campus = e.id_campus WHERE s.id_campus IS NULL ORDER BY e.id_building

queries.name: D07 · Students with no campus or with no degree
queries.description: Two anti-joins at once with OR: all the students have a valid campus and degree.
queries.sql: SELECT st.id_student FROM students AS st LEFT JOIN campuses AS s ON s.id_campus = st.id_campus LEFT JOIN degrees AS e ON e.code = st.degree_code WHERE s.id_campus IS NULL OR e.id_degree IS NULL ORDER BY st.id_student

queries.name: D08 · Repeated enrollments of the same student/subject pair
queries.description: GROUP BY + HAVING over the M:M: there are no duplicated pairs, the natural key is unique.
queries.sql: SELECT m.id_student, m.id_subject, COUNT(*) AS times FROM enrollments AS m GROUP BY m.id_student, m.id_subject HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

queries.name: D09 · Grades outside the 0–10 range
queries.description: Business rule over the grade range: none outside 0–10.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL AND (grade < 0 OR grade > 10)

queries.name: D10 · Invented enrollment statuses
queries.description: NOT IN against the list of allowed statuses: only active, passed and cancelled exist.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, status FROM enrollments WHERE status NOT IN ('active', 'passed', 'cancelled') ORDER BY id_enrollment

queries.name: D11 · Passed enrollments with no grade
queries.description: The rule «passed ⇒ grade reported»: no passed enrollment is left without a grade.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, status, grade FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'passed' AND grade IS NULL ORDER BY id_enrollment

queries.name: D12 · Graded enrollments that are not passed
queries.description: The other way round: if there is a grade, the enrollment is passed (active and cancelled are not graded).
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, status, grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL AND status <> 'passed' ORDER BY id_enrollment

queries.name: D13 · Classrooms with no seats
queries.description: Business rule: every classroom offers at least one seat.
queries.sql: SELECT id_classroom, code, capacity FROM classrooms WHERE capacity <= 0 ORDER BY id_classroom

queries.name: E01 · Simple view: SELECT * of another query
queries.description: The result of A03 is read as a table: the 5 large classrooms with their three columns (code, capacity, floor), sorted by capacity.
queries.sql: SELECT * FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] ORDER BY capacity DESC, code

queries.name: E02 · Arithmetic over the columns of a view
queries.description: The capacity is still a number after going through view A03: it can be divided by 10 and the remainder computed.
queries.sql: SELECT code AS classroom, capacity, capacity / 10 AS tens, capacity % 10 AS remainder FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] ORDER BY capacity DESC, code

queries.name: E03 · WHERE and DISTINCT over a view
queries.description: It filters view A03 by capacity >= 60 and leaves the distinct floors: floors 1 and 3 are left.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT floor FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] WHERE capacity >= 60 ORDER BY floor

queries.name: E04 · Aggregates over a view
queries.description: Five aggregates in one row over the result of A03: 5 classrooms, 320 seats, from 55 to 80 and an average of 64.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS classrooms, SUM(capacity) AS seats, MIN(capacity) AS min_grade, MAX(capacity) AS max_grade, ROUND(AVG(capacity), 2) AS average_grade FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)]

queries.name: E05 · Floors with two or more large classrooms
queries.description: It groups view A03 by floor and keeps the floors with two or more classrooms: only floor 1 (4 classrooms, 240 seats).
queries.sql: SELECT floor, COUNT(*) AS classrooms, SUM(capacity) AS seats FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] GROUP BY floor HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY floor

queries.name: E06 · View joined to a base table (INNER JOIN)
queries.description: View C02 joined to the subjects table by id_subject: the 8 subjects with four or more students, with their year and credits.
queries.sql: SELECT c.subject, c.students, a.year, a.credits FROM [C02 · Subjects with four or more students (large group)] AS c INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = c.id_subject ORDER BY c.students DESC, c.id_subject

queries.name: E07 · Two views joined by subject
queries.description: Views C02 and A31 joined by id_subject: the 6 large subjects that also have an average grade.
queries.sql: SELECT c.subject, c.students, n.average_grade FROM [C02 · Subjects with four or more students (large group)] AS c INNER JOIN [A31 · Average grade per subject (HAVING and ORDER BY by alias)] AS n ON n.id_subject = c.id_subject ORDER BY c.students DESC, c.id_subject

queries.name: E08 · Table LEFT JOIN view with IS NULL
queries.description: LEFT JOIN of the buildings table against view B08 plus IS NULL: the only building with no classrooms, the Sports Pavilion.
queries.sql: SELECT e.id_building, e.name AS building FROM buildings AS e LEFT JOIN [B08 · Classrooms and seats per building] AS v ON v.id_building = e.id_building WHERE v.classrooms IS NULL ORDER BY e.id_building

queries.name: E09 · View of a view (two levels of query)
queries.description: It reads view E05, which in turn reads view A03: three chained levels and a single row (floor 1, 240 seats).
queries.sql: SELECT floor, classrooms, seats FROM [E05 · Floors with two or more large classrooms] WHERE seats >= 100 ORDER BY seats DESC

queries.name: E10 · The same view twice (self-join)
queries.description: View A03 appears twice with different aliases and joins itself by capacity: only P-101 and P-102 tie at 55 seats.
queries.sql: SELECT a.code AS classroom_1, b.code AS classroom_2, a.capacity FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] AS a INNER JOIN [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] AS b ON b.capacity = a.capacity AND b.code > a.code ORDER BY a.capacity DESC, a.code, b.code

queries.name: E11 · Implicit join with commas including a view
queries.description: Cartesian product of view B06 with the campuses table, filtered by campus 1: the 6 degrees with their credits, from most to least.
queries.sql: SELECT c.code, c.degree, c.credits, s.name AS campus FROM [B06 · Subjects and credits per degree (join by a text code)] AS c, campuses AS s WHERE s.id_campus = 1 ORDER BY c.credits DESC, c.code

queries.name: E12 · ORDER BY by alias and LIMIT over a view
queries.description: It sorts by the alias subject and cuts view C02 to 3 rows: the three subjects with 5 students.
queries.sql: SELECT subject AS materia, students FROM [C02 · Subjects with four or more students (large group)] ORDER BY students DESC, subject LIMIT 3

queries.name: E13 · Boolean going through a view
queries.description: The boolean is_main travels untouched from the campuses table to view A01: only North Campus is the main one.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS campus, is_main FROM [A01 · All campuses] WHERE is_main = true ORDER BY id_campus

queries.name: E14 · Nulls going through a view (COALESCE)
queries.description: The missing phone of campus 3 is still null after reading view A01, and COALESCE replaces it with «no phone».
queries.sql: SELECT name AS campus, COALESCE(phone, 'no phone') AS contact FROM [A01 · All campuses] ORDER BY id_campus

queries.name: E15 · Aggregates over a view that is already aggregated
queries.description: It summarises the already aggregated view A32 (one row per campus): 4 campuses, 24 students and between 3 and 9 per campus.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS campuses, SUM(students) AS students, MIN(students) AS minimum, MAX(students) AS maximum FROM [A32 · Students and addresses per campus]

queries.name: E16 · A view that reads a query with LIMIT
queries.description: View C13 carries LIMIT 5: reading it as a table brings only those 5 rows (23 enrollments in all).
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, SUM(enrollments) AS enrollments FROM [C13 · Subjects with more enrollments (ORDER BY of an aggregate)]

queries.name: E17 · A view of an empty result
queries.description: View C10 returns no rows: reading it as a table gives an empty table, and COUNT(*) returns 0 instead of an error.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows FROM [C10 · Nobody takes subjects of two degrees (only rowCount)]

queries.name: E18 · LIMIT and OFFSET over a view
queries.description: LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2 over the 5 rows of view A03: the third, fourth and fifth classrooms by capacity.
queries.sql: SELECT code, capacity FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] ORDER BY capacity DESC, code LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2

queries.name: E19 · LIKE filter over a view
queries.description: LIKE over a column of view A03: the only large classroom whose code starts with K.
queries.sql: SELECT code, capacity FROM [A03 · Large classrooms (>= 55 seats)] WHERE code LIKE 'K%' ORDER BY code

queries.name: E20 · A view of a view that joins two views
queries.description: It reads view E07 (which joins C02 and A31) and keeps the average grades of 7 or more: 4 subjects.
queries.sql: SELECT subject, students, average_grade FROM [E07 · Two views joined by subject] WHERE average_grade >= 7 ORDER BY average_grade DESC, subject

queries.name: E21 · LEFT JOIN between two views
queries.description: C02 LEFT JOIN A31: the large subjects that do not reach the HAVING of A31 (Computer Networks and Public Health) come with a null average_grade, the first ones.
queries.sql: SELECT c.subject, c.students, n.average_grade FROM [C02 · Subjects with four or more students (large group)] AS c LEFT JOIN [A31 · Average grade per subject (HAVING and ORDER BY by alias)] AS n ON n.id_subject = c.id_subject ORDER BY n.average_grade ASC NULLS FIRST, c.subject

queries.name: E22 · Projection with an alias and an asterisk over a view
queries.description: The asterisk of the alias (v.*) over view A04: the 10 classrooms with a projector, with their two columns.
queries.sql: SELECT v.* FROM [A04 · Classrooms with a projector] AS v ORDER BY v.capacity DESC, v.code

queries.name: E23 · A view that reads a query with three tables
queries.description: View B02 joins three tables inside (campuses, buildings and classrooms): reading it as a table brings its 3 rows.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows FROM [B02 · Three tables: large classrooms of campus 1]

queries.name: E24 · Group by a boolean of a view
queries.description: GROUP BY over a boolean that comes from view A15: how many level/officialness combinations there are of each kind.
queries.sql: SELECT is_official, COUNT(*) AS combinations FROM [A15 · Level/officialness combinations (DISTINCT of two columns)] GROUP BY is_official ORDER BY is_official

queries.name: F01 · Students with an active enrollment (IN with a subquery)
queries.description: IN with a subquery: the students whose identifier shows up in the inner SELECT.
queries.sql: SELECT id_student, last_name FROM students WHERE id_student IN (SELECT id_student FROM enrollments WHERE status = 'active') ORDER BY id_student

queries.name: F02 · Students with no enrollment (NOT IN with a subquery)
queries.description: NOT IN with a subquery: only the students nobody enrolled anywhere.
queries.sql: SELECT id_student, last_name FROM students WHERE id_student NOT IN (SELECT id_student FROM enrollments) ORDER BY id_student

queries.name: F03 · Subjects with no enrollment (NOT IN with a subquery)
queries.description: The subjects that do not appear in any enrollment.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name FROM subjects WHERE id_subject NOT IN (SELECT id_subject FROM enrollments) ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: F04 · Campuses with a building of more than four floors (EXISTS)
queries.description: EXISTS with a correlated subquery: it is checked again for every campus.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_campus, c.name FROM campuses AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM buildings AS b WHERE b.id_campus = c.id_campus AND b.floors > 4) ORDER BY c.id_campus

queries.name: F05 · Campuses with no building of more than four floors (NOT EXISTS)
queries.description: The other side of the previous example: NOT EXISTS keeps the campuses with no match.
queries.sql: SELECT c.id_campus, c.name FROM campuses AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM buildings AS b WHERE b.id_campus = c.id_campus AND b.floors > 4) ORDER BY c.id_campus

queries.name: F06 · Degrees with a scholarship student (EXISTS, correlated)
queries.description: The subquery points at the outer degree (d.code): a correlated EXISTS.
queries.sql: SELECT d.code, d.name FROM degrees AS d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students AS s WHERE s.degree_code = d.code AND s.has_scholarship = TRUE) ORDER BY d.code

queries.name: F07 · Databases enrollments better than some Data Structures grade (> ANY)
queries.description: x > ANY (…) is true when the grade beats at least one of the inner values.
queries.sql: SELECT id_enrollment, grade FROM enrollments WHERE id_subject = 2 AND grade > ANY (SELECT grade FROM enrollments WHERE id_subject = 1) ORDER BY id_enrollment

queries.name: F08 · The highest credits of the first year (>= ALL)
queries.description: x >= ALL (…) needs the comparison to hold for every inner value: only the top credits pass.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name, credits FROM subjects WHERE credits >= ALL (SELECT credits FROM subjects WHERE year = 1) ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: F09 · Subjects with no researcher teacher (<> ALL)
queries.description: x <> ALL (…) is the same as x NOT IN (…): it keeps the values that differ from every one of them.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name FROM subjects WHERE id_teacher <> ALL (SELECT id_teacher FROM teachers WHERE is_researcher = TRUE) ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: F10 · Students with a scholarship
queries.description: This query is not a test by itself: it is the view the next examples read inside a subquery.
queries.sql: SELECT id_student, last_name, degree_code FROM students WHERE has_scholarship = TRUE

queries.name: F11 · Scholarship students read from the view (subquery over a view)
queries.description: The subquery reads the view F10 as if it were a table: [F10 · …] inside the IN.
queries.sql: SELECT s.id_student, s.last_name FROM students AS s WHERE s.id_student IN (SELECT id_student FROM [F10 · Students with a scholarship]) ORDER BY s.id_student

queries.name: F12 · Average grade per subject of 8 or more (derived table)
queries.description: A subquery in the FROM with an alias (t) is a derived table: it is queried like any other table.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_subject, t.avg_grade FROM (SELECT id_subject, AVG(grade) AS avg_grade FROM enrollments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL GROUP BY id_subject) AS t WHERE t.avg_grade >= 8 ORDER BY t.id_subject

queries.name: F13 · Subjects with four or more enrollments (derived table and JOIN)
queries.description: The derived table is joined to the subjects table and its column total is filtered.
queries.sql: SELECT t.id_subject, a.name, t.total FROM (SELECT id_subject, COUNT(*) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY id_subject) AS t INNER JOIN subjects AS a ON a.id_subject = t.id_subject WHERE t.total >= 4 ORDER BY t.total DESC, t.id_subject

queries.name: F14 · Enrollments of every student of a campus (scalar subquery in SELECT)
queries.description: The subquery in the column list returns one value per row: the enrollments of that student.
queries.sql: SELECT s.id_student, s.last_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments AS m WHERE m.id_student = s.id_student) AS enrollments FROM students AS s WHERE s.id_campus = 4 ORDER BY s.id_student

queries.name: F15 · Subjects above the average credits (scalar subquery in WHERE)
queries.description: The subquery returns a single value (the average) that the WHERE compares with.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name, credits FROM subjects WHERE credits > (SELECT AVG(credits) FROM subjects) ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: F16 · Degrees with five or more students
queries.description: A query whose SQL carries a subquery also works as a view: this one uses a correlated EXISTS with HAVING.
queries.sql: SELECT d.code, d.name FROM degrees AS d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students AS s WHERE s.degree_code = d.code HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5) ORDER BY d.code

queries.name: F17 · The previous view read as a table
queries.description: F16 is read from the FROM like a table, even though inside it there is a subquery.
queries.sql: SELECT code, name FROM [F16 · Degrees with five or more students] ORDER BY code

queries.name: F18 · Subjects of degrees with a scholarship student (nested subqueries)
queries.description: One subquery inside another: the inner one picks the degrees and the outer one the subjects.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.id_subject, a.name FROM subjects AS a WHERE a.degree_code IN (SELECT s.degree_code FROM students AS s WHERE s.has_scholarship = TRUE) ORDER BY a.id_subject

queries.name: F19 · Subjects that do not reach the top credits (NOT with ALL)
queries.description: NOT (… >= ALL (…)) is the negation of the ALL predicate: everything but the top ones.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name FROM subjects WHERE NOT (credits >= ALL (SELECT credits FROM subjects WHERE year = 1)) ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: F20 · Buildings of the main campus (= ANY)
queries.description: x = ANY (…) is the same as x IN (…): it is kept for completeness of the quantifiers.
queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT b.id_campus FROM buildings AS b WHERE b.id_campus = ANY (SELECT id_campus FROM campuses WHERE is_main = TRUE) ORDER BY b.id_campus

queries.name: F21 · Subjects with more credits than some Primary Education one (> SOME)
queries.description: SOME is a synonym of ANY: the comparison has to hold for at least one inner value.
queries.sql: SELECT id_subject, name FROM subjects WHERE credits > SOME (SELECT credits FROM subjects WHERE degree_code = 'GEDU') ORDER BY id_subject

queries.name: G01 · Campus and degree names, without repeats
queries.description: UNION of two tables with one column each: the campus names and the degree names, every one once and sorted by name.
queries.sql: SELECT name FROM campuses UNION SELECT name FROM degrees ORDER BY name

queries.name: G02 · The country of every campus, twice (UNION ALL)
queries.description: The same SELECT on both sides of UNION ALL: the rows are stacked without removing repeats, so there are 8 of them.
queries.sql: SELECT country FROM campuses UNION ALL SELECT country FROM campuses ORDER BY country

queries.name: G03 · Every country once (UNION)
queries.description: The same union without ALL: UNION removes the repeated rows, so each country comes out once.
queries.sql: SELECT country FROM campuses UNION SELECT country FROM campuses ORDER BY country

queries.name: G04 · A union read as a table
queries.description: The union goes in the FROM with an alias (derived table): the subject identifiers of the catalogue and of the enrollments, without repeats, are counted.
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT id_subject FROM subjects UNION SELECT id_subject FROM enrollments) AS t

queries.name: G05 · Union with output alias, ORDER BY and LIMIT
queries.description: Both sides name their column item: the ORDER BY of the union sorts the combined result by that name and the LIMIT keeps the first 5.
queries.sql: SELECT name AS item FROM buildings UNION SELECT code AS item FROM classrooms ORDER BY item LIMIT 5
